Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Mei (Redwood SE), Anika (Redwood CSM), Evan (CTO, Riftstream), Priya (DevOps), Sam (ML)

Summary:
Quick ignition sync to confirm access paths, pilot scope (embeddings + generation for internal knowledge), and next steps for private deployment. Heavy focus on VPC peering, KMS, and Dedicated capacity sizing. Some notes on caching (they said KV cash a few times) and sample traffic shape.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick us off. quick round robin?
[00:10] Evan: Evan here, CTO at Riftstream, thanks. we want to get the pilot moving this week ideally.
[00:18] Priya: Priya, I'll be doing the VPC side and the VPN. a lot of our infra constraints are around egress and private subnets.
[00:27] Sam: Sam, ML eng — i'll share sample prompts and perf targets.
[00:33] Mei: Mei, Redwood SE — i'll own the Dedicated sizing discussion and run the initial throughput run.
[00:38] Anika: Anika, CSM — i'll track docs and next steps.

[01:05] Jordan: Goal for today: confirm who needs access, how we do the network path (VPC peering vs transit), initial model choices, and a follow-up dedicated sizing sess.
[01:26] Evan: Perfect. main use case is internal knowledge assistant + embeddings for search, some high-urgency generated summaries. latency target sub-300ms on critical paths, cost needs to be kept reasonable.
[01:49] Mei: Ok good. quick question on context length — you mentioned 8k tokens in the intake, is that the typical window?
[02:04] Sam: yeah 8k is target for now; a couple of teams might go to 16k later but pilot stays at 8k.

[02:40] Priya: On networking — we prefer VPC peering to keep traffic internal, and we have strict egress rules, we also need to lock down IPs.
[03:02] Jordan: Great, we'll send the VPC peering checklist. note that for Redwood Private we can do customer-managed VPC with a private control plane. Mei, can you cover the routing options?
[03:20] Mei: Sure. routing wise we support direct peering or IPsec VPN. direct peering is lower latency, but depends on their provider support; we recommend direct peering if customer accepts our peering ranges. you mentioned egress whitelisting — we'll provide static egress IPs for the cluster.
[03:45] Priya: Good — do you publish those IP ranges? we need them for firewall rules.
[03:52] Jordan: yes we'll attach the ranges to the checklist.

[04:10] Evan: Security big ask: KMS/HSM keys and audit logs. our compliance team requires key ownership, not only encryption in transit.
[04:26] Anika: we have integrations with customer-managed KMS and HSM. Jordan will share the KMS integration doc after the call.
[04:38] Mei: for audit logs — Redwood Console exposes per-request traces and you can route logs to your S3 or SIEM, or we can do a push to their ingestion endpoint.

[05:05] Sam: On the model side — we're leaning to an open 8k model you have listed, we might want quantized variants for cost savings. any constraints on custom weights?
[05:22] Mei: We support model artifacts you bring, but for private deployments there are compatibility checks — we run a quick validation to ensure operator kernels match; also we provide Redwood-verified builds for common open models which is faster.
[05:40] Jordan: For the pilot let's pick Redwood-verified 8k variant to avoid initial onboarding friction, then test customer model later.

[06:18] Priya: What's the flow to SAML/SSO? we want RBAC mirroring from Okta.
[06:30] Anika: We support SAML/SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and role sync. We'll give a mapping template so you can align Okta groups to Redwood roles.
[06:46] Evan: Great. also need audit-ready logs for who invoked the model and tokens used per request.

[07:10] Mei: On performance — two levers: Dedicated GPU pools vs Hosted. Dedicated buys you predictable throughput and lower P99 latency. We can show initial cost tradeoffs in the sizing session. Also caching — prefix caching and KV cache (sometimes transcribed as KV cash) reduce tokens for repeated context.
[07:40] Sam: How intrusive is the prefix caching to response correctness? we rely on fresh context for summaries.
[07:55] Mei: Caching is optional and workload-aware; for freshness-critical calls we avoid prefix caching. for embeddings we recommend a local cache for hot vectors.

[08:20] Jordan: On SLA and legal — we will share the SOC2 pack and the standard ILAs. Evan, do you have procurement timelines?
[08:34] Evan: We'd like pilot signed in two weeks, procurement and legal want security docs out this week.
[08:45] Jordan: We'll prioritize the security pack. Anika will send SOC2, network and KMS docs by Wed.

[09:10] Priya: A note on routing — we have a transit hub and prefer to peer with our transit VPC. will that work?
[09:22] Mei: Yes transit peering is fine; routing is a config detail. we'll add a section to the peering checklist for transit hub architectures.

[10:00] Sam: For benchmarking — we'll run a small scale benchmark on your verified 8k model. how do we run it? do you provide a harness?
[10:12] Mei: We'll provide a simple k6 / python harness and sample payloads. For Dedicated, we can run an internal micro-benchmark on a staging cluster to show P50/P95/P99.
[10:28] Jordan: I'll include the harness and a short spreadsheet template for traffic shape input.

[11:02] Evan: About data retention — we need to ensure no customer data is stored beyond defined retention for the pilot. can you set retention policies?
[11:18] Anika: Yes retention windows are configurable per deployment — we'll document defaults and how to change them.

[11:40] Priya: Also TLS termination — can we bring our certs?
[11:46] Mei: In Private you can manage certs; in Dedicated we also support customer certs via our cert injection process.

[12:05] Jordan: Quick recap: Redwood to send security pack, VPC checklist + egress IPs, KMS guide, and the harness. Schedule Dedicated sizing with Mei and Sam. Priya to provision test VPC. Pilot scope: embeddings + generation on verified 8k model.

[12:35] Evan: Sounds good. any blockers on our side today?
[12:40] Priya: i'll need the IP ranges and checklist to configure firewalls, so that's the only blocker.
[12:47] Jordan: We'll get that by 2027-03-24.

[13:10] Sam: one last question — do you support per-route throttles to protect against runaway prompts?
[13:18] Mei: yes rate limits and per-token quotas per API key, and you can set soft and hard limits. We also have cost alerts in Redwood Console.

[13:42] Anika: i'll follow up with calendar invites for the sizing session and the onboarding ticket.
[13:49] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll share the artifacts.

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription sometimes mislabels technical terms (KV cash instead of KV cache, peering ranges typed as IP ranges - occasional word swap). There's some crosstalk during network bits.

End of transcript.
